forecast.reasoning: South Africa's ADCI (49.1) is unchanged for a second straight week, and this week's evidence reinforces rather than resolves the central open question: FIN-01 (7.26, still the dataset's lowest score) sits against a strong, independently-corroborated digital-finance picture -- Chainalysis's own regional report now confirms South Africa as the #2 Sub-Saharan African crypto market by dollar volume, alongside the pilot's best Government pillar (76.2) and strong Infrastructure (84.3). Base case holds: this construct mismatch persists through 2030 absent a registry revision, meaning South Africa's headline ADCI likely continues to understate its actual digital-finance maturity. Upside case is now more concrete than last cycle: if FIN-02 access is resolved (a specific global Chainalysis rank located, or a documented fallback construct adopted per this week's Red Team Finding 4), South Africa's Finance pillar likely improves further given its confirmed strong regional standing -- this is no longer speculative, it's a data-access problem with identifiable fixes. Downside case is unchanged: continued VC cooldown (H1 2026 at $83M, missing $100M) softening ECO-01/ECO-02 from an already-weak base.

Nigeria's ADCI (53.2) is unchanged for a second straight week and remains the pilot's most complete dataset (10 of 10 indicators). Base case is unchanged from last cycle: FIN-01's registration-based construct (49.5) and FIN-02's rank-based conversion (96.7, confirmed stable at rank #6 this cycle, no further correction needed) continue on their current trajectories, with NIN enrollment progressing toward its 82%-by-end-2026 target. Upside case still hinges on whether the H1 2026 equity-funding reversal ($214M, first continental equity lead since 2022) holds through a full year -- no fuller-year data has emerged yet to confirm or deny this, so the case is carried forward unchanged rather than strengthened or weakened. Downside case is unchanged: GOV-02 (53.7, lowest of the three pilot countries) remains the clearest structural drag if e-government service delivery does not improve.

Kenya's ADCI (48.8) is unchanged for a second straight week. This cycle's most consequential finding is methodological, not numerical: GOV-01's stale 2024 base is now confirmed, via a direct check of immigration.go.ke, to reflect a genuine primary-source reporting gap rather than lazy secondary citation -- three consecutive cycles have failed to locate a fresher figure by any method. Base case is nudged slightly down from last cycle (54 to 53) to reflect that this is looking less like a temporary data lag and more like a durable measurement problem that will keep GOV-01 understated (and low-confidence) for the foreseeable future unless Kenya's government changes its own reporting practices. Upside case unchanged in substance but now conditional on something more specific: a change in *government reporting behavior*, not just Claude searching harder. Kenya's FIN-01 strength (52.6, still the pilot's best on a like-for-like usage basis) continues independent of the GOV-01 story, per prior Integration notes -- M-Pesa's rail predates and doesn't depend on Maisha Namba. Downside case unchanged: continued institutional friction plus a weak H1 2026 VC showing, still unconfirmed against a fuller-year figure, compounding an already-weak Economy pillar.
